def: A test collection that many people agree to use, so that results from different papers and products can be compared.
A benchmark of 18 English datasets from 9 retrieval tasks, scored by nDCG@10, for testing zero-shot generalisation of retrievers.
The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: eight embedding task types over dozens of datasets and many languages, whose retrieval part reuses BEIR.
The massively multilingual extension of MTEB, with over 500 tasks in more than 250 languages and a cheaper downsampled version.
Testing a model on data it was not trained on, to estimate how it will behave on a new corpus.
Overlap between a model's training data and a benchmark's test data, which inflates the model's score.
Judgements collected from term-matching systems favour term-matching systems, so semantic retrievers look worse than they are.
A benchmark built for one field, such as finance or reasoning-heavy queries, used to check how far general results transfer.
Using a public benchmark to choose a few candidates to test on your own data, rather than to make the final decision.
